title: Khronos BoomBox -- a real metal-rough asset whose stated appearance IS its emissive image

criterion.says: A common object with glowing front panel created with Core glTF 2.0.
criterion.note: KHRONOS'S OWN WORDS NAME THE GLOWING FRONT PANEL, AND THAT PANEL IS ONE IMAGE. The material states emissiveFactor [1, 1, 1] and puts the whole of the glow in emissiveTexture, so a renderer that read the factor and not the image emits white over the entire body -- the criterion inverted rather than missed. That is what this case is here to show, and it is readable from the picture: the panel is lit and the rest of the box is not. SUBJECT CLASS IS DERIVED: 0.10820033856560365 of 1280x720 = 99716 px^2 over 6036 triangles counted by the magnitude of their signed area is 16.5 px^2 per triangle over both sides of a closed body, about 8 px^2 on the side facing the camera, so no part of this subject is sub-pixel.

acceptanceClass.because: A fronto-parallel planar placement owns three continuous freedoms -- two of aim and one of scale -- and every distinct silhouette line costs one condition, so 2 + k >= E is what decides whether the construction can be written at all (`board/`). A curved fetched body of 6036 triangles resolves into thousands of distinct lines and no roll makes any of them rational; the acceptance is therefore worst_disagreement_px against the oracle's own filter half-width, which introduces no constant of its own.

subjects.name: BoomBox
subjects.notes: The binary spelling, so the images travel inside the one file the store is keyed on. A SUPPLIED TANGENT, which is the half of the normal-map question our generator never reaches: `Subject` must not regenerate one, and this asset is where a real exporter's basis crosses.

source.pinReason: the corpus's single pin; every Khronos subject in the tree is read at this commit so that one bump moves all of them

blender.note: A release version, not a commit. Recorded so a red rung can be attributed to our renderer or to the oracle, and carried in the oracle's cache key so a version bump misses instead of serving a stale render. We do not aim to be bit-identical with Cycles.

camera.derivation: The framing rule of board:0083 (src/gltf/Framing.h) applied to this subject's own bounds and to nothing else: azimuth 35 deg and elevation 20 deg in glTF's +Y-up frame, distance r / sin(yfov/2) / 0.6 about the AABB's centre, yfov = 2*atan(12/50) from Blender's factory 50 mm lens on a 24 mm sensor height at sensor_fit VERTICAL, near = distance - r and far = distance + r. THE ROLL IS ZERO AND STATED: this subject's silhouette is not rational at any roll, so a roll would be a different draw of the same lottery rather than an exactness argument.
camera.note: THE ENGINE'S OWN ANSWER, QUOTED (board:1398). Every number here is read from the framing rule's output for this subject -- eye, aim, yfov and both clip planes -- rather than recomputed by the authoring helper, which bounded each primitive by the eight transformed corners of its local AABB and therefore always at least as loosely as the engine bounds the transformed vertices. A looser radius moves the eye back, and 93 cases declared a camera the rule does not derive. `ADerivedCameraIsTheFramingRuleAndNotAQuotation` recomputes all of it and refuses a mismatch, so what this declaration does is PIN the viewpoint, never choose it.

light.note:
A DELTA LIGHT AND NOT AN ENVIRONMENT, and on a metal-rough asset that is what makes the row decidable at all: a uniform environment delivers the same radiance from every direction, so roughness, metalness and the normal map all stop changing the picture. IRRADIANCE pi W/m^2 IS DERIVED AND NOT CHOSEN: a Lambertian white facet facing the beam returns rho*E/pi = 1, so the picture is scene-referred around unity and no exposure decides whether it is legible. THE ANGULAR DIAMETER IS ZERO AND THE RUNNER REFUSES ANYTHING ELSE -- a sun with an angle is a disc, which is an area source, an estimator in the oracle and a soft terminator no punctual light draws. THE BEAM IS SLANTED OFF THE VIEW AXIS -- the framing rule puts the eye at azimuth 35 deg and elevation 20 deg, and a light down the same axis is a headlight that flattens every form the row is supposed to shape.

THE SUBJECT'S OWN SURFACE IS NOT A SECOND SOURCE, AND THAT IS A REDUCTION OF THE ORACLE RATHER THAN A TOLERANCE ON IT. This material declares an emissiveTexture, so Cycles used to carry its triangles in the light tree beside the sun and pick one per shading event: MEASURED between seed 0 and seed 1 under this exact recipe, 55 496 binary colour samples -- one side exactly zero -- over a body whose alpha channel was identical in both. The preparer now takes it out of the light tree AND out of the one BSDF-sampled direction the integrator still traces at zero bounces; the second half is not optional here, since the first alone left 42 samples over 15 pixels where a sampled direction found the lit speaker ring. Two seeds, same recipe, after: 0.

world.note: BLACK, AND THAT IS THE REDUCTION RATHER THAN A LOOK. Blender's factory world is an area source Cycles samples, which at one sample per pixel is a Bernoulli draw rather than a value. With the world at zero the only source left is a light with no area, the estimator has no variance, and the two seeds must agree bit for bit.

material.note:
THE FILE'S OWN ROW ENTIRE, and it has to be: the subject IS the material stack, and every arm that LOWERS the closure -- a diffuse or an emissive one -- throws away everything but one image. The file states base colour, metallic-roughness, normal and emissive in four images and this arm binds all four.

WHAT THE ORACLE HAS AND WE DO NOT IS VISIBILITY. Cycles traces a shadow ray per shading event, so its render of this asset carries the body's own shadow; `render/stages/SubjectDraw.h` states in its own words that neither arm computes visibility, so ours does not. THAT DIFFERENCE IS IN THE PICTURE AND IT IS NOT A TOLERANCE: this case is `self-describing`, the image residual is printed and decides nothing, and what is judged is the placement exactly and the appearance by eye.

default.note: One sample per pixel with the box filter at its RNA minimum makes Cycles evaluate the same coverage predicate a centre-sampling rasteriser does. The only source is a light with no area over a world of strength zero, so the estimator has no variance left and the two seeds must agree bit for bit.

seed-shift.note: The same recipe at another seed, and the whole of what the reduction is accepted on. The only source in this scene is a sun of angular diameter zero over a world of strength zero, and the subject's own surface is no longer one -- `emission_sampling = NONE` takes it out of the light tree and its ray visibility takes it out of the one BSDF-sampled direction the integrator still traces at zero bounces -- so the oracle has no estimator left and the two dumps must agree bit for bit. Any difference NAMES the source that still gathers.

subjectFrameFraction.note: The fraction of the frame the subject's projected area covers at frame 0, RE-HARVESTED after the camera became the framing rule's own answer (board:1398). Recomputed by the runner on every run and refused on mismatch, so this line PINS the framing and never chooses it; seeded from that recomputation, it is a drift detector rather than a present-error check.
